picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Missouri-Ole Miss Winner After Changing His Pick on Air Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Rece Davis expected to be the only voice backing No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss on Saturday, but the College GameDay host changed his prediction after ESPN’s Dan Wetzel and Pete Thamel both took the Tigers first. Davis made his pick on the College GameDay Podcast . He’s forecasting a back-and-forth game in Oxford that ends with the Rebels holding off former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons and the Tigers. Why Rece Davis switched his pick Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) hands the ball off to running back Makhi Frazier (25) against the Vanderbilt Commodores | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis came into the segment leaning toward Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). That’s the same side ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took earlier this week . Davis came into the segment leaning toward Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). That’s the same side ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took earlier this week . “You guys have surprised me because I thought for sure I was going to be the only one to pick Missouri,” Davis said. “I’m going to change my mind a little bit. Not just because you guys took Missouri, but I was leaning Missouri. Austin Simmons’ revenge, running game, the whole thing.” Davis also pointed to Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz, saying “a lot of times when Drink hits the mic, sometimes it doesn’t work out as well for the Tigers.” His forecast echoes Sept. 26, when Missouri gave up a fourth-quarter lead in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. “A back-and-forth game, up and down. Probably ends up much like Missouri’s last trip to the state of Mississippi,” Davis said. “I’ll say the Rebels hang on. I’ll be the one who says the home team wins it.” Missouri’s top-10 history at stake Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Missouri has rolled since that loss. The Tigers routed No. 8 Florida 45-17 , giving Drinkwitz his first regular-season win over a top-10 team in 11 tries at Missouri, and then beat Texas A&M 27-6. Missouri has rolled since that loss. The Tigers routed No. 8 Florida 45-17 , giving Drinkwitz his first regular-season win over a top-10 team in 11 tries at Missouri, and then beat Texas A&M 27-6. “If Missouri can do it, having a top-10 win because the Gators were top 10 at the time, they can win multiple games against top-10 teams for the first time since 1978,” Davis said. That 1978 team shut out defending national champion Notre Dame 3-0 and beat No. 2 Nebraska 35-31. Simmons lost Ole Miss’ starting job after a Week 2 ankle injury against Kentucky in 2025. At Missouri, the left-hander has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns and one interception, which is one yard fewer than Trinidad Chambliss has for the Rebels. Tigers running back Jamal Roberts leads the SEC in rushing. He’ll face an Ole Miss run defense that ranks last in the conference at 176.4 yards allowed per game and 106th nationally in EPA per rush allowed . “The Ole Miss defense hasn’t been what we thought it was going to be,” Davis said. “I remember talking to some people in the preseason, thinking this might be one of the best defensive fronts in college football. Maybe it’ll turn out to be, but so far we haven’t seen evidence of that.” How can Ole Miss hang on? Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) counters with Chambliss, a Heisman Trophy contender who’s back for another season after he won an injunction against the NCAA , and running back Kewan Lacy, who began his career at Missouri. “There’s also a little bit at stake here in the personal rivalry for Trinidad Chambliss, too. Maybe Kewan Lacy,” Davis said. Lacy set Ole Miss’ single-season record with 1,567 rushing yards in 2025 and signed a deal to return to Oxford . Still, his health hangs over this week. A shoulder injury kept him out of the 52-28 loss at Florida, and he left last week’s 52-17 win at Vanderbilt after seven carries. The Rebels’ offense ranks eighth nationally in success rate, while Missouri’s defense has allowed 23 points total across its last two games. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET on SEC Network, and the loser falls to 2-2 in SEC play. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. Golding called Lacy's return in any capacity a "best-case scenario." Lacy had carried seven times for 39 yards and a touchdown against Vanderbilt before leaving the game during a period when Ole Miss had established a comfortable lead. He was absent from the injury report ahead of the Missouri contest, making him available for the meeting with his former program. away.headline: Ahmad Hardy injury update: Star Missouri football RB not yet back in practice
away.blurb: Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz said that there currently is no change to the Mizzou football running back's injury status during his press availability Tuesday, Oct. 13. Drinkwitz said that Hardy has not yet started a two-week ramp-up period that he needs to see for the running back to return to the field. Drinkwitz, as recently as last Tuesday, said that he'd provide an update as soon as one was available. But rumors began to swirl on various online platforms Monday night, including PowerMizzou at 247Sports and on Reddit, that Hardy may be close to a return to practice. Drinkwitz was again asked about Hardy's current status on Tuesday. The message board poster has become quite popular for a string of Mizzou predictions over the past year, some of which have panned out. "If he practices, I promise, I'll tweet it out. I won't even give it to Pete (ESPN reporter Pete Thamel)," Drinkwitz said. "We'll just do it ourselves. So, again, I think it's going to be really important — I know everybody's excited about where we're at and all that good stuff. When he's available, I promise you we'll be excited to use him. But that's not the story right now. So, nothing new." Mizzou has its idle week after the game against the Rebels. That technically means that if Hardy is able to return to practice sometime this week, he would be in a position to possibly return for Mizzou's next game Oct. 31 at Arkansas. away.headline: Pete Golding knows Austin Simmons is 'scary' as Missouri QB returns to Ole Miss
away.blurb: “It’s fun watching him develop as the season goes. Obviously had two games under his belt here and then got hurt. You see him getting better week-in, week-out. Relating it back to when he was here, there’s certain things you gotta go back from a scrimmage standpoint and all those things, what affected him what didn’t affect him.” Simmons, who opened 2025 as Mississippi’s starter before being replaced by Trinidad Chambliss due to injury, is enjoying a breakout season at Missouri. The 6-foot-4 quarterback has 1,434 passing yards with 14 touchdowns to one interception this season while leading the Tigers to a 5-1 record and No. 13 ranking in the US LBM Coaches Poll . Golding said Ole Miss will have its hands full slowing down Simmons and Missouri’s offense on Saturday. He also said it’s a bit scary having more context than most into Simmons’ rise. “It’s scary to know how good he is and how talented he is,” Golding said at his weekly news conference. “Love Austin, did an unbelievable job while he was here. He’s got elite arm talent, always has. More athletic than you think. Both Golding and Missouri are hoping familiarity plays a role in the outcome of No. 13 Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC) vs. No. 10 Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1). Here's what to know of Simmons' reunion with the Rebels: Why did Austin Simmons transfer from Ole Miss? Simmons opened last season with 341 passing yards and three touchdowns to two interceptions in Ole Miss’ 63-7 win over Georgia State. Only a week later, the promising first-year starting quarterback injured his ankle against Kentucky, opening the door for Chambliss, the backup quarterback, to take the reins in Oxford. Unfortunately for Simmons, Chambliss — a relative unknown at the time after transferring from Division II Ferris State over the offseason — never gave them back. He eventually led Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff semifinals after emerging as one of the best quarterbacks in college football. Simmons ultimately entered the transfer portal on Jan. 2 before signing with the Tigers four days later, on Jan. 6. He stayed with Ole Miss throughout its CFP run, but decided to move schools, especially with the program expecting Chambliss to gain another season of eligibility for the 2026 season at the time. Former Ole Miss coach Lane Kiffin, who’s now at LSU, said in 2025 that Simmons and Chambliss made up "the best quarterback room in the country." "I think Austin (Simmons) is a great quarterback, was playing really well for a first-time starter, and I think he'd be having a great year if he was still in there. I have all the confidence in the world in him," Kiffin said on Nov. 11, 2025. "So I think we have two that are better than a lot of people's No. 1." That’s likely why Missouri was comfortable handing the offense over to a quarterback with only two career starts before 2026. Why did Austin Simmons choose Missouri? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings One of college football's great rivalries takes center stage on Saturday night when No. 3 Miami welcomes Florida State for their traditional October clash Getty Images Get ready for one of college football's most bitter rivalries when No. 3 Miami welcomes Florida State at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday for their traditional October clash. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications , though this season those conversations are focused far more on the Hurricanes, who finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender. Where to watch Miami vs. Florida State live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 7 p.m. ET Location : Hard Rock Stadium -- Miami Gardens, Florida TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation. Florida State struggling against top teams : While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami. No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026 : The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest ) was decided by less than 28 points. Miami vs. Florida State prediction, picks Miami isn't just blowing teams out on the scoreboard this season; it's a team that's also been exceeding oddsmakers' expectations nearly every week. The Hurricanes indeed have the best point differential in FBS (+39.8), but they also rank T-14 nationally with a 4-1 record against the spread and carry the 15th-best cover margin in the country, beating the spread by an average of 7.8 points per game. With those kinds of trends, it's tough to think that Miami is a candidate for an upset alert, and Florida State's road woes make it very possible that this game will get sideways on the Seminoles. picks.headline: Florida State @ Miami Preview And Prediction
picks.blurb: Florida State @ Miami Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Rays take 3-2 ALCS lead Zero carries for Cam Miami, BYU are 1-2 Fantasy Basketball sign up Caleb delivers in return Florida State @ Miami Preview And Prediction Oct 3, 2026; Clemson, South Carolina, USA; Miami Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) celebrates a first down during the third quarteragainst the Clemson Tigers at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Ashley Tumlin-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 9:10 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 3 Miami looks unstoppable heading into its rivalry showdown with Florida State. Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. How Each Team Wins For Miami, the formula is simple: establish the run, protect the football, and allow Mensah to attack Florida State's secondary. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. Final Score: No. 3 Miami 45, Florida State 20 Miami remains undefeated, improves to 6-0, and strengthens its national championship case. Meanwhile, the pressure on Mike Norvell reaches another level following another disappointing rivalry performance. Check Out All EasySportz College Football Content Here! picks.blurb: Predicting the No. 3 Miami Hurricanes Starter at Right Guard Against Florida State Seminoles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Rays take 3-2 ALCS lead Zero carries for Cam Miami, BYU are 1-2 Fantasy Basketball sign up Caleb delivers in return (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Anthony Aguirre Sat, October 17, 2026 at 3:10 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads MIAMI, Fla. – Ahead of Saturday night's in-state rivalry matchup against the Florida State Seminoles , the No. 3 Miami Hurricanes will have a new starting right guard. Sophomore Max Buchanan will be sidelined for an extensive portion of the season. He was injured in the Hurricanes' 41-13 win over Clemson at Death Valley (Memorial Stadium). Despite returning to finish the game, Buchanan underwent surgecal repairs. Given the Hurricanes' cross-training for offensive linemen, head coach Mario Cristobal will have a plethora of options. The big question: Who does he trust the most? It won't be revealed until kickoff, but here are candidates looking to take the starting role, plus a final prediction. After Buchanan initially went down against the Tigers, it was the fellow sophomore who stepped in. Alofaituli lost his starting role at left guard to freshman Max Buchanan. The 21-year-old logged 32 offensive snaps and finished with a 55 pass-protection Pro Football Focus grade. However, Alofaituli didn't allow a sack, pressure, hit, or hurry. He played the entirety of the Hurricanes' nine-play touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, which they exclusively ran the ball. However, Alofaituli doesn't have the traditional size for a guard. He's listed at 6-2 and 298 pounds. It's proven to be a weakness at times and the Seminoles could exploit if Alofaituli is lined up at right guard. It's been a slow freshman campaign for the former elite five-star recruit. Cantwell has logged just 78 offensive snaps through five games. As both starting tackle roles are occupied by veterans Samson Okunlola (left) and Matthew McCoy (right), the only real opportunities for the 18-year-old to play is in the interior. Cantwell has 59 snaps at right guard, but carving out a rotational role has been a different challenge. The Nixa (Mo.) native will very likely play at tackle as early as next season, but right guard is currently up for grabs. Cantwell could seize the moment, unless this final candidate has something to say about it. The Georgia transfer joined the Coral Gables program with experience all over the line of scrimmage, except center. Meriweather has played in a reserve role, but could be the closest to climbing the depth chart. In the Hurricanes' 52-3 win over Central Michigan, he logged 28 snaps and all were at right guard. Meriweather finished with an 83.3 pass-protection PFF grade. Similar to Cantwell, the redshirt junior is naturally a tackle, but he's shown comfortability in playing in the interior. Joining Okunlola, McCoy, and center Ryan Rodriguez at the line of scrimmage is Meriweather, educationally guessed by Roundtable Sports beat writer Anthony Aguirre. He has tremendous and versatile experience, which can benefit the Hurricanes' protection unit. picks.headline: Important Notes: No. 3 Miami Hurricanes Vs. Florida State Seminoles Preview, Injury Report, and More
picks.blurb: Important Notes: No. 3 Miami Hurricanes Vs. Florida State Seminoles Preview, Injury Report, and More - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NHL Fantasy Hockey Stanley Cup Final World Juniors Rays take 3-2 ALCS lead Zero carries for Cam Miami, BYU are 1-2 Fantasy Basketball sign up Caleb delivers in return (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Anthony Aguirre Sat, October 17, 2026 at 1:24 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads MIAMI, Fla. – In less than 12 hours, the No. 3 Miami Hurricanes will kick off against the Florida State Seminoles for the 71st time in the Sunshine State's rivalry history. Both programs are powerhouses and multiple National Championship winners, but it's different this time around. The Seminoles have progressively declined since the 2023 13-1 season; meanwhile, the Hurricanes are on the brink of fully reclaiming former glory. Here is what's most important to know before Saturday night's game: Television Channel: ESPN Kickoff Time: 7:00 p.m. E.T. The Hurricanes are -2000 favorites to win and the Seminoles have a +1000 chance to pull off an upset. The spread is at -20.5 and the over/under is at 50.5. The following Hurricanes players are ruled out: Wide receiver Joshua Moore (Upper-Body; Out for Season), running back CharMar "Marty" Brown (Left Leg; Out for Season), cornerback Ja'Boree Antoine (Undisclosed), right guard Max Buchanan (Left Knee), cornerback Romans "OJ" Frederique Jr. (Left Shoulder), and tight end Luka Gilbert (Undisclosed; Out for Season). Junior cornerback Xavier Lucas is set to return from a four-game absence. Star edge rusher Marquise Lightfoot, linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr., and cornerback Damari Brown were banged up ahead of the bye week, but aren't listed on the injury report. The following Seminoles are ruled out: Running back Samuel Singleton Jr., wide receiver Devin Carter, safety Karson Hobbs, linebacker Blake Nichelson, cornerback Jamari Howard, linebacker Izayia Williams, cornerback Jordan Crutchfield, and linebacker Daylen Green. Freshman linebacker Noah LaValle was listed as questionable on the initial injury report, but has been officially ruled out. Meanwhile, edge rusher Darryll Desir and center Paul Bowling are probable. The Seminoles have the second-most rushing attempts in the Atlantic Coast Conference; meanwhile, the Hurricanes have the best run defense in the Football Bowl Subdivision. Sophomore running back Ousmane Kromah is a great offensive threat. He's second in the ACC with 565 rushing yards on 100 carries and scored five touchdowns. Kromah is among the nation's leaders with 38 forced missed tackles. As the Hurricanes' front seven looks to be at full strength, the 20-year-old will meet with swarmers. Seminoles' fifth-year quarterback Ashton Daniels will need to dispute all early narratives this season. He has one of the lowest completion percentages (59.5) among ACC starters. The Hurricanes will likely look to force Daniels to throw more while simultaneously stopping the run – a similar game plan against Clemson and freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds. However, where Daniels lacks in passing, the 22-year-old makes up for on the gound. He leads the ACC with 10 rushing touchdowns. Defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman has a fair amount of experience in facing dual-threat quarterbacks and finding success. The Hurricanes have the highest-scoring offense (averaging 49.6 points) in FBS; meanwhile, the Seminoles have the 20th worst total defense. It should be a lopsided matchup at Hard Rock Stadium, but rivalrly games can get interesting. You could argue that the biggest surprise of the college football campaign is that Mike Norvell is still employed by Florida State . There is the whole $46.7 million buyout that looms, and the Seminoles are also searching for their next athletic director, but FSU seems destined for its third consecutive losing season and its fifth in Norvell's seven years in Tallahassee. The shouts for Norvell's axing are likely to get louder this week as the Seminoles travel to No. 3 Miami as 21.5-point underdogs before hitting their bye week. If Florida State is blown out for the second straight week, it could be curtains for Norvell. It is almost certainly delaying the inevitable, but I think the Seminoles may be able to avoid getting embarrassed at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday. I'm not saying that Florida State will win, or even make Miami sweat it out, but the Seminoles are competent enough to keep this thing within three scores. It's a low bar, I know. away.headline: Florida State Seminoles’ heartbreaking loss to Miami gets even worse with star RB injury update
away.blurb: Florida State's loss to No. 3 Miami was painful enough on its own. Then came the injury news. Running back Ousmane Kromah will be out for an extended period, a major blow for a Seminoles team that is now 3-4 overall and 1-3 in ACC play. Kromah was carted off late in the second quarter with a left ankle injury after a 9-yard run to the Miami 2-yard line. He had 14 carries for 44 yards at the time. An air cast was placed on his left leg, and he did not return. Florida State Seminoles’ heartbreaking loss to Miami gets even worse with star RB injury update - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints Sun, October 18, 2026 at 4:35 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Seminoles lost 43-35 in double overtime. Miami's Darian Mensah threw for 326 yards and three touchdowns, including a 3-yard strike to Malachi Toney in the second overtime. Florida State entered as a 21-point underdog but repeatedly erased deficits and tied the game at 14, 21 and again in regulation. Duce Robinson delivered a 75-yard touchdown that tied the game with 2:49 left in regulation. He added a 20-yard score to open the first overtime. Florida State appeared to give itself another chance when Ashton Daniels connected on a fourth-and-21, 36-yard heave that would have made it 43-41. A holding penalty brought it back. The game ended with Bryce Fitzgerald's end-zone interception, amid FSU's claims that the final play should have been a touchdown. Daniels scored on the next play to tie the game at 14-14 at halftime. The team never had its top rusher again. Quintrevion Wisner and Amari Thomas would be in line for more touches. Florida State will now have to find a way to replace its lead back during a difficult stretch of the schedule. Reports during the game described the injury as an ankle or left leg problem, and no official diagnosis had been released in the sources reviewed. The extended-absence update makes the loss to Miami even more painful. away.headline: Miami vs Florida State live updates: Hurricanes, Seminoles head to OT
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: Ashton Daniels kneeled out the clock, and we're headed to overtime. The teams will alternate possessions starting at the opponents' 25-yard line. If it goes to a second overtime, teams will have to go for 2 if they score a touchdown. After that, the teams will trade 2-point conversion tries until there's a winner. In his first game back since the opener at Stanford, cornerback Xavier Lucas made what could turn out to be the biggest play of the game. Tre Wisner got loose on a long run, but Ethan O'Connor stripped the ball loose, sending the ball skidding across the wet grass. Lucas fell on it to give Miami the ball at its own 39. Darian Mensah may not be having his best game, but he is still showing impeccable touch on some difficult throws. He got a throw out just before Rylan Kennedy could get to him, lofting a 19-yard looper to Vandrevius Jacobs. As the fourth quarter begins, the Canes have the ball at the FSU 20. Miami outgained FSU 149-76 in the third quarter, but the visitors benefitted big time on two turnovers (one on downs). UM can't afford to miss here if they want to stay undefeated. One play after Ousmane Kromah was carted to the locker room with a devastating ankle injury, Ashton Daniels took it in himself for the game-tying touchdown from 2 yards out. He held up three and two fingers to shout out Kromah's number 32 after the score. With FSU driving again and the 2-minute timeout having just passed, Chase Smith wrapped up Ousmane Kromah by the ankles. The running back was injured on the play, and trainers brought out an air cast for him. He was carted off the field. The Seminoles were already without Sam Singleton Jr. entering the game; without Kromah, among the top-20 running backs in the nation with 565 yards entering the game, Texas transfer Tre Wisner becomes their main RB. After a Miami three-and-out, Ashton Daniels returned to the game and looked like he didn't miss a beat, scrambling for 10 yards on a third-and-8. Later, he dumped a screen pass over three rushing Hurricanes to tight end Dessirio Riles for a 23-yard touchdown to tie it up. FSU is averaging 6.1 yards per play against a banged-up Miami defense. Ashton Daniels scrambled for 14 yards. As he slid, safety Zechariah Poyser hit him in the head area, bringing out a flag for the personal foul. His ejection for targeting was upheld upon review. That play and Bryce Fitzgerald's injury leaves an already depleted Miami secondary without two more starters. Xavier Lucas got injured in the opener vs. Stanford and hasn't played since, but he's expected to be back in the starting lineup tonight. O.J. Frederique also has been out since Week 1 but needs more time to return, leaving either Damari Brown, Ethan O'Connor or converted safety Bryce Fitzgerald starting opposite Lucas against FSU. home.headline: Miami vs Florida State live updates: Hurricanes, Seminoles head to OT
home.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
home.blurb: Ashton Daniels kneeled out the clock, and we're headed to overtime. The teams will alternate possessions starting at the opponents' 25-yard line. If it goes to a second overtime, teams will have to go for 2 if they score a touchdown. After that, the teams will trade 2-point conversion tries until there's a winner. In his first game back since the opener at Stanford, cornerback Xavier Lucas made what could turn out to be the biggest play of the game. Tre Wisner got loose on a long run, but Ethan O'Connor stripped the ball loose, sending the ball skidding across the wet grass. Lucas fell on it to give Miami the ball at its own 39. Darian Mensah may not be having his best game, but he is still showing impeccable touch on some difficult throws. He got a throw out just before Rylan Kennedy could get to him, lofting a 19-yard looper to Vandrevius Jacobs. As the fourth quarter begins, the Canes have the ball at the FSU 20. Miami outgained FSU 149-76 in the third quarter, but the visitors benefitted big time on two turnovers (one on downs). UM can't afford to miss here if they want to stay undefeated. One play after Ousmane Kromah was carted to the locker room with a devastating ankle injury, Ashton Daniels took it in himself for the game-tying touchdown from 2 yards out. He held up three and two fingers to shout out Kromah's number 32 after the score. With FSU driving again and the 2-minute timeout having just passed, Chase Smith wrapped up Ousmane Kromah by the ankles. The running back was injured on the play, and trainers brought out an air cast for him. He was carted off the field. The Seminoles were already without Sam Singleton Jr. entering the game; without Kromah, among the top-20 running backs in the nation with 565 yards entering the game, Texas transfer Tre Wisner becomes their main RB. After a Miami three-and-out, Ashton Daniels returned to the game and looked like he didn't miss a beat, scrambling for 10 yards on a third-and-8. Later, he dumped a screen pass over three rushing Hurricanes to tight end Dessirio Riles for a 23-yard touchdown to tie it up. FSU is averaging 6.1 yards per play against a banged-up Miami defense. Ashton Daniels scrambled for 14 yards. As he slid, safety Zechariah Poyser hit him in the head area, bringing out a flag for the personal foul. His ejection for targeting was upheld upon review. That play and Bryce Fitzgerald's injury leaves an already depleted Miami secondary without two more starters. Xavier Lucas got injured in the opener vs. Stanford and hasn't played since, but he's expected to be back in the starting lineup tonight. O.J. Frederique also has been out since Week 1 but needs more time to return, leaving either Damari Brown, Ethan O'Connor or converted safety Bryce Fitzgerald starting opposite Lucas against FSU. AccuWeather predicts 80 degrees with thunderstorms possible at kickoff in Miami Gardens, Florida. Winds are expected to blow out of the north at 8 mph. There's about a 70% chance of rain and storm

Two teams coming off massive upset victories will collide Saturday night as No. 15 Kentucky (5-1) travels to Norman to face Oklahoma (3-2) in a crucial SEC matchup. Kentucky is coming off a thrilling 35-34 overtime victory over LSU, while Oklahoma stunned Texas 27-24 in the Red River Rivalry. Both programs have plenty to prove, but the biggest question is whether Oklahoma can build on its impressive victory and finally establish some consistency. Kentucky: Can the Wildcats Keep Rolling? Kentucky has been one of the SEC's biggest surprises under first-year head coach Will Stein. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has thrown for 1,394 yards and 11 touchdowns, while running back CJ Baxter has rushed for 484 yards and eight scores. Baxter was outstanding against LSU, rushing for 123 yards and two touchdowns. The Wildcats are averaging nearly 35 points per game, but Oklahoma's defense presents a completely different challenge. Brent Venables has built one of the nation's most physical defensive units, allowing just 17.6 points and approximately 267 yards per game. If Kentucky cannot establish Baxter early, Minchey could face constant pressure throughout the evening. Oklahoma: The Defense Is Carrying This Team Oklahoma's victory over Texas was impressive, but the Sooners still have serious offensive concerns. Quarterback John Mateer has thrown for 1,038 yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Against Texas, Mateer managed just 155 passing yards, and Oklahoma needed a blocked punt touchdown and multiple defensive stops to secure the victory. However, the Sooners' defense has been outstanding. Oklahoma is allowing just 150 passing yards per game, making life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. With Adepoju Adebawore creating pressure up front, the Sooners have the personnel to disrupt Kentucky's offense. If Mateer can avoid turnovers and Oklahoma establishes any consistency running the football, the Sooners should have enough offensive production to win. How Each Team Wins Kentucky must establish Baxter early, protect Minchey, and avoid giving Oklahoma short fields through turnovers. The Wildcats also need to force Mateer into obvious passing situations. For Oklahoma, everything starts defensively. The Sooners must contain Baxter, pressure Minchey, and create opportunities for their offense. Playing in Norman should also provide a significant advantage for Venables' team. I expect Kentucky to keep this game competitive, but Oklahoma's defense will ultimately make the difference. The Wildcats should find some success moving the football, particularly early, but sustaining long drives against this Sooners defense will be extremely difficult. Mateer won't need to deliver a spectacular performance. Instead, Oklahoma will rely on its defense, field position, and a few explosive offensive plays. Expect Kentucky to threaten late before Oklahoma comes up with one final defensive stop. Final Score: Oklahoma 27, No. 15 Kentucky 21 The Sooners build on their Red River victory, improve to 4-2, and keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. It's just assumed that Texas will find its way into the College Football Playoff, and maybe get to the SEC Championship first. But it just lost to an Oklahoma team that pulled off an all-time found-a-way 27-24 win in the Red River Rivalry. The Sooners only have one SEC loss – 41-13 to Georgia – but all of a sudden, the second half of the schedule doesn't seem that bad. Kentucky, because it's in the first year of the Will Stein era, and Oklahoma, because it beat Texas – both programs are in a good place. But the winner of this will still be alive in the SEC, and the other almost certainly won't. Kentucky vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes on the road for two of the next three weeks, traveling to Mississippi State, hosting South Carolina, and going to Florida. It's a key stretch for Kentucky with Vanderbilt at home next, followed by a date at Tennessee. The two programs have only met three times. Oklahoma won 29-8 in 1982 and 29-7 in 1980, but Bear Bryant's Kentucky won the 1951 Sugar Bowl. Start here – it's just not screwing up. UK turned it over three times in the loss to Alabama, twice in a win over South Alabama, and that's it. No turnovers on the road at Texas A&M and South Carolina, and none last week against LSU. And then there are the penalties – there aren't any. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and fewest penalty yards, and that matters. The lack of turnovers matters. It all matters, because Oklahoma probably can't pull this off without the Wildcats royally screwing up like Texas did last week. Why Oklahoma Will Win Kentucky needs its running game to rock, and that's going to be a problem. Georgia was able to power away on Oklahoma with a few big runs in the blowout win, but that's been about it. Michigan tried to run a lot, and it did just enough to get by, but it was a struggle. Texas wasn't exactly creative in the way it tried to run, and it got stuffed way too often. The Sooners are 3-0 when they don't allow a touchdown run, and 0-2 when they do. Oklahoma will hold up defensively in a low-scoring game that comes down to a few key late stops, but this won't be easy for a team that failed to hit 300 yards of total offense against anyone but UTEP. Kentucky is 135th in the nation in third down conversions. Oklahoma is third in the nation in third down stops. And that's the ball game. Broadcast Details - TV: SEC Network and ESPN Unlimited (Dave Neal, Cole Cubelic and Tori Petry) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) What You Need To Know NORMAN, Okla. — Oklahoma gets its first real chance to prove the Texas win was more than one loud night in Dallas. The Sooners host No. 15/17 Kentucky on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. in Norman, and the setup could not be much cleaner for a measuring-stick home opener in SEC play. Oklahoma is 3-2 and 1-1 after knocking off No. 1 Texas on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky is 5-1 and 3-1 after beating No. 10 LSU in overtime. Both teams are coming in hot. Only one of them gets to leave Norman still feeling like the week actually changed something. That is the whole tone of this game. Oklahoma does not need another moral victory. It already got the statement result in the Cotton Bowl. Now the question is whether Brent Venables ' team can stack a second one against a ranked opponent at home, in throwbacks, with the building expecting the version of the Sooners that showed up after halftime in Dallas. The storyline writes itself. Oklahoma just beat the top team in the country. Kentucky just survived LSU 35-34 in overtime for its second straight 35-34 overtime win. Will Stein's group is not sneaking into Norman quietly. This is Kentucky's highest AP ranking since 2022, and the Wildcats are playing with the kind of confidence that makes road environments less intimidating than they used to be. Stein's background adds a little spice too. He was on Texas' staff from 2015 to 2017, then spent the last three years as Oregon's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach while the Ducks made the College Football Playoff. He knows big stages. More importantly for Saturday, he has a quarterback in Kenny Minchey who takes care of the ball, extends plays, and has already shown he can finish tight games. Oklahom a's recent history after Texas also hangs over the night. Since 1999, the Sooners are 25-2 in the game immediately following the Red River rivalry. The only losses in that stretch were to Kansas State in 2014 and South Carolina in 2024. That is a real trend, but trends do not tackle Minchey or cover Kentucky's skill players. Oklahoma still has to earn the next one. If the Sooners are going to control this game, it starts where most of their best football has started all year: on defense. Oklahoma is allowing just 12.8 first downs per game, best in the country. The Sooners also rank among the national leaders in third-down defense, red-zone defense, passing defense, total defense, and sacks. Opponents have scored on only 15 of 62 possessions. The second-half numbers are even tighter. Oklahoma has given up just 27 points after halftime all season, including only three in the third quarter. That profile matters against a quarterback like Minchey. He is efficient, hard to rattle, and dangerous when the pocket breaks down. Oklahoma cannot afford soft edges or impatient linebackers. The formula is the same one that showed up against Texas: keep contain, force longer developing throws, win early downs, and make Kentucky drive the hard way. The Sooners are 11-2 under Venables when they score a defensive touchdown, including 4-0 since the start of last season. They do not need another pick-six Saturday. They do need the same disruptive identity. The personnel is built for it too. All 14 defensive starters began their college careers at Oklahoma. Owen Heinecke has been the tone-setter again, leading the team in tackles in four of five games. Peyton Bowen just took over a rivalry game. Courtland Guillory made the late interception that set up the Texas winner. The front still has Taylor Wein, David Stone, Danny Okoye, and enough depth to keep the pressure coming. If that group plays clean, Oklahoma has a real chance to dictate the night. The uncomfortable truth is that Oklahoma's offense is still looking for consistency even after the biggest win of the season. The Texas game gave the Sooners a blueprint more than a finished product. They scored in all three phases, finally got some second-half juice on the ground through Lloyd Avant, and did just enough in the passing game when the moment arrived. John Mateer did not have to play hero ball. Isaiah Sategna still created the biggest throws on the final drive. Rocky Beers continues to look like one of the smarter portal additions on the roster, ranking among the national leaders in receiving yards per game by a tight end. That is the version Oklahoma needs again. Not perfect. Just complementary. The red-zone efficiency has been solid, and the explosive pass plays are still there. What has lagged is the ability to stay on schedule without leaning so hard on the defense and special teams. Kentucky's defense has not been elite by the numbers, but Venables already made clear that "relief" is not the word inside the building. Every week is still about Oklahoma getting better. The offensive line remains one of the quieter swing factors. Michael Fasusi has been working back from the shoulder injury that knocked him out after the opener, and any step toward getting the line more whole helps the whole operation. Avant gave the run game a pulse against Texas. Xavier Robinson and Tory Blaylock still have to become more reliable pieces if Oklahoma wants drives that do not feel like they are always one negative play from stalling. There are plenty of side notes around the game, and most of them favor the home team if Oklahoma plays like it should. The Sooners are wearing the Bud Wilkinson-era throwbacks again. Memorial Stadium has been a fortress since 1999, with a 153-17 record and a sellout streak that never seems to blink. Venables is 2-2 in conference home openers. The roster has true veteran captains across both sides of the ball. Special teams, once a liability, now look like a genuine strength with Tate Sandell , Grayson Miller, and Doug Deakin's unit playing with confidence. But the schedule context is what keeps this from feeling comfortable. Oklahoma has already seen Michigan, Georgia, and Texas. Still left are Kentucky, Mississippi State, Ole Miss, and Missouri among the ranked or dangerous remaining names. This is not a soft landing after Dallas. It is the next hard one. Kentucky is good enough to punish a flat home team, especially if Minchey gets into a rhythm and Oklahoma's offense stalls early. That is why Saturday matters beyond one week in the standings. The Texas win stopped the spiral and put Oklahoma back in the conversation. A home win over a ranked Kentucky team would make that conversation real. A letdown would turn Dallas back into an isolated highlight instead of the start of a run. The Sooners do not need to look perfect. They need to look intentional. Defend with the same edge that has carried them all year. Run the ball well enough to keep the game clean. Let Mateer manage instead of force. Protect the edges against Minchey. And finish the night like a team that understands the standard is no longer just competing in these games. Oklahoma has the defense. It has the home field. It has the momentum. Kentucky has the confidence of a team that has already won a couple of ugly, important games. Saturday night in Norman should tell us which one is actually building something.

By Cory Nightingale Published: Oct 15, 2026 · 5:07 PM EDT The Inside College Football crew gave its pick earlier this week for the huge SEC matchup on Saturday in Norman between No. 15 Kentucky and Oklahoma. The Wildcats are the ranked team among the 2 teams, coming in at No. 15, but the Sooners have their own momentum going despite being unranked after last week's stunning victory over then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. That means we have 2 teams who'll be coming into the Week 7 primetime clash with some serious good feeling. No. 15 Kentucky is 5-1 overall and on a 4-game winning streak, capped by back-to-back overtime wins over South Carolina and LSU by the exact same 35-34 score. The Cats are 3-1 in the SEC, with their lone conference setback against Alabama in Week 2 feeling like a long time ago. Then there is Oklahoma, which suffered through a 2-2 September that took it from the AP rankings straight out of those rankings. But the win over Texas last week at the Cotton Bowl could be a season saver, with the 3-2 Sooners trying to gain momentum through the middle of the season. The Cats and Sooners will kick off on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on SEC Network, and the CBS Sports analysts on Inside College Football had their own thoughts on the Week 7 showdown. Let's just say Aaron Taylor, Rick Neuheisel and Brian B.J. Jones all had their own vision of what will happen in Norman, and the trio didn't land on the same team when making their picks. picks.headline: How No. 15 Kentucky football & Oklahoma match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Having led Kentucky to back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins, Kenny Minchey is proving himself a cool customer under game-deciding stress. Two weeks ago at South Carolina, Minchey had running back CJ Baxter make a pre-snap shift so he could pick up an otherwise-free edge rusher. As the block was achieved, Minchey threw the game-winning two-point-conversion pass. Last week, Minchey realized the LSU defense had a Grand Canyon-sized hole in the middle of its formation. On a called pass play, the Hendersonville, Tennessee, product instead ran right through that hole for the game-winning two-point-conversion run. On the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey is completing 67.4% of his passes and has thrown for 1,394 yards with 11 touchdown throws vs. one interception. • Oklahoma’s John Mateer began the season on the outskirts of the Heisman Trophy discussion but has so far had a rough go in 2026. Ball security has been a problem for the 6-1, 224-pound Mateer. He threw a crucial interception late in Oklahoma’s 17-10 loss at Michigan in Week 2. He also turned the ball over three times in the first half at Georgia on Sept. 26, helping the Bulldogs open a 28-0 halftime lead en route to a 41-13 win. In Oklahoma’s 27-24 upset of then-No. 1 Texas last week, however, Mateer completed 18 of 26 passes for 155 yards with no interceptions. Mateer has not been as effective a rusher so far in 2026 as he has been in past seasons. Through five games, Mateer has a net-70 yards rushing. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky’s CJ Baxter ripped off a 77-yard run on UK’s first play from scrimmage in last week’s win over LSU. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, finished with 123 rushing yards on 19 carries against the Tigers. A transfer from Texas, Baxter is fifth in the SEC in rushing with 484 yards. Third-year player Jason Patterson has carried only seven times combined in the past two games after suffering an apparent injury at South Carolina. A 5-10, 204-pound product of Sneads, Florida, Patterson had been one of UK’s breakout players over the season’s first four games. • Oklahoma’s ground game has, so far, been mostly stalled. The Sooners are last in the SEC in rushing, averaging only 95.8 yards a game. Lloyd Avant Jr ., a transfer from Colorado State who began his college career at Tulsa, leads the Sooners in rushing with 239 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries (an average of 4.5 yards a rush). Avant, however, had a strong showing in the win over Texas, rushing 10 times for 72 yards and a touchdown. Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby was named SEC Freshman of the Week for the second straight week after catching four passes for 79 yards, including two crucial receptions late in the game, in the win over LSU. On the season, Darby, a 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, is eighth in the SEC in receptions (29) and ninth in receiving yards (401). Ja’Kayden Ferguson had caught only three total passes in UK’s first five games, but the 6-2, 184-pound, second-year player made three key receptions in the win over LSU. “He made some unbelievable plays,” Will Stein said of Ferguson. “... He blocked hard. He played hard. He’s got a lot of talent, a lot of upside.” • Isaiah Sategna III has been Oklahoma’s most effective offensive skill player so far in 2026. The 5-10, 185-pound senior from Austin, Texas, has 25 catches for 331 yards and two touchdowns. Sategna caught five passes for 64 yards in the win over Texas. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez made a team-high six catches for 25 yards vs. LSU. A 6-4, 249-pound junior from Covington Catholic, Rodriguez is second on the UK team in receptions (28) and receiving yards (219). Henry Boyer had a quiet showing vs. LSU with one catch for four yards. The 6-6, 270-pound transfer from Illinois has only nine catches on the season, but those receptions have yielded 120 receiving yards and three touchdowns. • Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers is, like UK’s Rodriguez, one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. A 6-5, 240-pound senior from Littleton, Colorado, Beers has 22 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Beers had four catches for 29 yards vs. Texas. Hayden Hansen caught 30 passes for 254 yards and two TDs last season while playing for Florida. So far this season, the 6-8, 270-pound Hansen has five catches for 74 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even Offensive line • After having a rough go against Alabama in Week 2, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has consistently been playing solid football. “Malachi is a really-good football player,” Will Stein said. “The guy is 6-8, 330 pounds. He is gonna be, probably, a top three-round NFL draft pick in the next couple years. “ • The Oklahoma offensive front has been much-criticized amidst the Sooners’ offensive struggles, but the unit showed some signs of hope in the second half vs. Texas. Freshman Noah Best has emerged as the jack-of-all-trades on the OU offensive line, already logging starts this season at center and both guard positions. Defensive line • Kentucky nose guard Jamarrion Harkless was one of the unsung heroes of the win over LSU. The 6-3, 346-pound alumnus of Frederick Douglass High School made three tackles, 1.5 sacks, forced a fumble and had a quarterback hurry against Lane Kiffin’s Tigers. “I told (Harkless) ‘That’s how you have to play for us to be successful on defense, game in, game out,’” Will Stein said. • Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone is an interior force. The 6-3, 312-pound junior from Del City, Oklahoma, made five tackles in the win over Texas. On the season, Stone has 19 tackles, two tackles for loss and half a sack. Advantage : Oklahoma • Due to injuries, Kentucky starting linebackers Grant Godfrey and Bo Barnes had to be iron men vs. LSU. WLB Barnes made 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss, while MLB Godfrey made 10 stops vs. the Tigers. • Oklahoma MLB Owen Heinecke leads the Sooners in tackles (36), is tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (two) and is second in tackles for loss (4.5). A 6-1, 226-pound fifth-year player from Tulsa, Heinecke made nine tackles vs. Texas. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior strong safety Ty Bryant made six tackles and intercepted a pass vs. LSU. For the 6-foot, 196-pound Bryant, a product of Frederick Douglass High School, it was his sixth career pick. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols made seven tackles and successfully defended a pass vs. LSU. • Oklahoma strong safety Peyton Bowen returned an interception of Texas quarterback Arch Manning 42 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter last week. A 6-foot, 200-pound product of Corinth, Texas, Bowen has made 24 tackles on the season, leads the Sooners in pass breakups with four and also has a forced fumble and a sack. Special teams • Kentucky punt returner Brock Coffman brought an LSU kick back 55 yards for a touchdown last week. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui entered last week’s game 6 of 7 on field-goal attempts but went only 2 of 4 vs. LSU. However, after missing two makeable field goals in the fourth quarter last week, Zouagui came back to hit a 33-yard field goal with 12 seconds left in the contest to tie the game at 27 and force overtime. After Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara punted in UK’s first five games, the Cats turned to former starter Wilson Berry vs. LSU. On three punts, Berry averaged 40.1 yards and pinned LSU inside its 20-yard line once. • Oklahoma’s special teams are elite. Danny Okoye blocked a Texas punt last week that Dakoda Fields recovered in the Longhorns’ end zone for a touchdown. Isaiah Sategna III is second in the SEC in punt returning, averaging 18.57 yards a return. He had an 88-yard punt-return touchdown in the season opener vs. UTEP. Punter Jacob Ulrich is averaging 44.31 yards on 16 kicks and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line three times. Place-kicker Tate Sandell kicked a 47-yard field goal on the game’s final play to beat Texas last week. On the season, Sandell is 5 of 8 on field goals with a long make of 53 yards (which also came against Texas). away.headline: OU football's fatal flaw haunts Sooners again in collapse vs Kentucky
away.blurb: "We had plenty of opportunities there late into the third quarter to knock them out. We just weren't able to get it done.” With Michael Fasusi, Heath Ozaeta and Eddy Pierre-Louis out due to injury, Fodje was already playing out of position on a line filled with backups. Now, he was in clear pain. “I just listen to the trainers and him, what he’s telling them,” Venables said. “Some guys try to battle through that because they’re able to. He did all he could. If the trainers come over and say somebody’s out or somebody’s up, it goes according to what they say.” “That's just football,” offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said of the offensive line. “We had opportunities there at the end of the game to go win the football game, and I got to be better in those moments and those situations, putting those guys in a position to be successful, regardless of who's out there. “Whatever 11 we have out there, it is my sole responsibility to put those kids in position to go be successful,” Arbuckle said. “Move the ball down the field, capitalize in those situations, those opportunities, regardless of who was out there. I have to be really good about putting those guys in position to go make the plays, to win the football game. Multiple injuries on the offensive line were a critical factor in the team's late-game collapse. Offensive lineman Ryan Fodje played through an injury, allowing two sacks on a key fourth-quarter drive. Quarterback John Mateer threw three interceptions, including a costly pick-six with just over a minute remaining. NORMAN — Around the midpoint of the third quarter, Ryan Fodje was hurt. Clearly in pain, the second-year Oklahoma offensive lineman limped off the field. Already down three linemen, the training staff re-taped Fodje’s right leg on the sideline and he was back in the game shortly afterward. The Sooners’ offensive line , which held its own for most of Saturday night, unraveled late. Fodje, who struggled to move, allowed two sacks on a critical drive early in the fourth quarter. OU’s offensive line injuries and lack of depth was its fatal flaw in a 21-13 loss to No. 17 Kentucky in which the Sooners outplayed the Wildcats for almost three quarters. With the loss, OU fell to 3-3. The Sooners outgained Kentucky 346-230 but their offense failed to move the ball with any efficiency late due to a decimated offensive line and overall inconsistent decisions. “They made the plays when they needed to, and we weren't able to get it done as a staff or as a team,” said Sooners coach Brent Venables, who is now 58 games into his tenure in which offensive dilemmas are a common theme. OU finally pulled Fodje late, placing Peyton Joseph at left tackle. Venables was asked postgame about the decision to continue playing Fodje even though he was clearly not 100%. away.headline: Mailbag: How will CJ Baxter, other injuries affect Kentucky’s playoff outlook?
away.blurb: Baxter was listed as a game-time decision on the pre-Oklahoma availability report. He participated in warmups and was running sprints on the sideline throughout the game but didn’t actually play. If Baxter does experience any setbacks this week, it does feel like holding him out against Vanderbilt with a bye week to follow would be a wise choice since Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes can still carry the load at running back. Vanderbilt is winless in SEC play, but Kentucky must still be on alert this week. This team needs a bye week to rest a variety of injuries, but I would be wary about holding anyone out against the Commodores who can play at other positions with less depth. The linebacker depth should be helped by the return of Alex Afari, but he did not play in Oklahoma, even after a judge made him eligible on Friday. The injuries for backup linebacker Antwan Smith and backup nickel back Jaden Smith appear to be long-term issues, so do not expect them back soon. Wide receiver Nic Anderson’s status will be worth watching this week too after he appeared to reaggravate his arm/shoulder issue in Oklahoma. But for this Kentucky team, it wasn’t even the highlight of the month. Kentucky rode its opportunistic defense to a 21-13 win over Oklahoma to move to 6-1 on the season and 4-1 in SEC play. The No. 12 Wildcats are tied for first place in the SEC and seem likely to be slotted in a projected playoff spot when the committee releases its first ranking on Nov. 3, as long as Will Stein’s team takes care of business against Vanderbilt this week. Regardless of what happens from here, Stein has given Big Blue Nation reason to dream. The Wildcats are already bowl eligible, and that fact seems like an afterthought because of bigger goals in reach. Those bigger goals mean fans might not be simply content to ride the current high. To reach the playoff — and contend there — more improvements are needed. That balance is evident in this week’s UK football mailbag. You can submit questions each week via Twitter, Blue Sky or email. Waco Kid on X: Is this real life? What dimension did we magically travel into? It would be inaccurate to say Kentucky had never enjoyed a first seven games like these before, but this feels unprecedented for a couple of reasons. When Kentucky was 7-1 in 2018 with a winner-take-all-game for the SEC East against Georgia looming, the playoff only included four teams. It still didn’t feel like Kentucky had a shot to be included in the field. When Kentucky was 6-1 in 2007 with two top-10 wins on the resume and College GameDay headed to Lexington for the first time in program history, there was no playoff. There was just a single national championship game with teams picked by the BCS computer ranking. That team had just beaten the No. 1-ranked team (and eventual national champion), but there was still a general acceptance that it was unlikely Kentucky would make it through the second half without taking another loss. Starting guard Eddy Pierre-Louis remains doubtful to play. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen was downgraded to out. Backup offensive lineman Heath Ozaeta is doubtful. Finally, cornerback Jacobe Johnson, wide receiver Parker Livingstone, linebacker Taylor Heim, running back Xavier Robinson, tight end Trynae Washington, and wide receiver Trell Harris have been ruled out. We just weren't able to get it done.” With Michael Fasusi, Heath Ozaeta and Eddy Pierre-Louis out due to injury, Fodje was already playing out of position on a line filled with backups. Now, he was in clear pain. “I just listen to the trainers and him, what he’s telling them,” Venables said. “Some guys try to battle through that because they’re able to. He did all he could. If the trainers come over and say somebody’s out or somebody’s up, it goes according to what they say.” “That's just football,” offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said of the offensive line. “We had opportunities there at the end of the game to go win the football game, and I got to be better in those moments and those situations, putting those guys in a position to be successful, regardless of who's out there. “Whatever 11 we have out there, it is my sole responsibility to put those kids in position to go be successful,” Arbuckle said. “Move the ball down the field, capitalize in those situations, those opportunities, regardless of who was out there. I have to be really good about putting those guys in position to go make the plays, to win the football game. Multiple injuries on the offensive line were a critical factor in the team's late-game collapse. Offensive lineman Ryan Fodje played through an injury, allowing two sacks on a key fourth-quarter drive. Quarterback John Mateer threw three interceptions, including a costly pick-six with just over a minute remaining. NORMAN — Around the midpoint of the third quarter, Ryan Fodje was hurt. Clearly in pain, the second-year Oklahoma offensive lineman limped off the field. Already down three linemen, the training staff re-taped Fodje’s right leg on the sideline and he was back in the game shortly afterward. The Sooners’ offensive line , which held its own for most of Saturday night, unraveled late. Fodje, who struggled to move, allowed two sacks on a critical drive early in the fourth quarter. OU’s offensive line injuries and lack of depth was its fatal flaw in a 21-13 loss to No. 17 Kentucky in which the Sooners outplayed the Wildcats for almost three quarters. With the loss, OU fell to 3-3. The Sooners outgained Kentucky 346-230 but their offense failed to move the ball with any efficiency late due to a decimated offensive line and overall inconsistent decisions. “They made the plays when they needed to, and we weren't able to get it done as a staff or as a team,” said Sooners coach Brent Venables, who is now 58 games into his tenure in which offensive dilemmas are a common theme. OU finally pulled Fodje late, placing Peyton Joseph at left tackle. Venables was asked postgame about the decision to continue playing Fodje even though he was clearly not 100%. home.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! This is the season for an Oregon team that should be in full rock-and-roll mode at this point, but instead it's been one big, sad trombone of a season. The Ducks are still 3-2 with a not-that-horrible schedule the rest of the way outside of a trip to Ohio State. They lost to UCLA, but they can stay alive in the Big Ten title hunt with one more loss, even if an at-large CFP bid is likely gone with a third defeat and no Big Ten Championship. And they have to do it with Nebraska's former star quarterback, Dylan Raiola – maybe. Nebraska had Indiana cooked, but it turned the stove off too early. The Hoosiers rallied back for a 20-17 win, but that might have been more about the defending national champs not being as good this year than the Huskers being close to fantastic. However, winning in Eugene is still hard, and if Nebraska can do it, it's 6-1 with a favorable schedule – Ohio State comes to Lincoln – and all of a sudden, it's on the fast track to 10-2 – at least – and a possible at-large CFP bid. Nebraska vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon ends a good run of home games and goes to Illinois after this. After that, it hosts Northwestern before going to Ohio State. Nebraska starts a run of three road games in four dates, getting a week off before playing Washington, and then it's off to Illinois. The two have never played as Big Ten teams. Oregon won the last meeting 42-35 in 2017. The Huskers are 6-2 overall in the series, with the first win in 1952. How To Watch Nebraska vs Oregon Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 11:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Nebraska Will Win UCLA beat up, battered, and bruised Oregon last week. The Ducks might have knocked out Bruin quarterback Nico Iamaleava with a knee injury, but they were destroyed offensively with seven turnovers and just 272 yards of total offense. Oregon is a mess. Star quarterback Dante Moore is expected to miss another game after suffering a concussion against USC. Dylan Raiola might get his shot against his former team, but he was beyond awful against UCLA. Brock Thomas doesn't have Raiola's talent, but he got the offense moving in the second half. Nebraska gave up two huge touchdowns against Indiana, but held firm the rest of the way. Oregon's offensive problems won't all of a sudden be fixed this week. Oct 10, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea (10) passes against the Indiana Hoosiers during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Why Oregon Will Win Lost in all of Oregon's misery is a defense that showed up and tried to save the day against UCLA. It's been the only team able to stuff the Bruin running game, and it should do the same against Nebraska, starting by keeping quarterback Anthony Colandrea from doing much on the move. The Huskers can force takeaways – three against Michigan State, two against Maryland – but the Ducks are capable of getting their running game moving a bit to take the pressure off the passing game. And about the quarterback situation, yes, Bob Chesney and the UCLA defense pitched a gem last week. But the week before that, Raiola stepped in and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns in a brilliant fill-in performance for Moore against USC. Now the Huskers travel up to Oregon for a 10 p.m. CT matchup, the latest start time for Nebraska since 2014. But other factors in this game make this clash all the more questionable. Dante Moore is out for the game, meaning Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas or even Akili Smith Jr. will be earning the start. But Raiola is the most poetic option after all and is likely the starter despite a rough outing against UCLA. After going 19-of-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, Raiola only threw 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions against the Bruins . He also got strip-sacked in the game. Though it was Raiola's only sack, UCLA still brought the pressure throughout. Raiola's main weakness is pressure, which the Bruins exploited last week. Though Raiola can find ways to stay alive in the pocket and deliver big plays, he rarely takes off downfield and has found himself in rough spots. Thomas took over in the fourth quarter for the Ducks and went 11-of-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown. He did, however, fumble on his opening drive but nearly completed the comeback. But even if Thomas starts, it remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success, especially after seeing Raiola's two-game stretch. Now, Nebraska can get to the quarterback, but the concern comes down to the explosive plays. Indiana pulled off multiple explosive plays last week, despite its struggle to produce points and yardage for most of the game. The Ducks can do the same, especially late in the game. Nebraska ran out of steam in the fourth against Indiana at home early in the afternoon. Now, the Huskers face Oregon on the road after dark. The Ducks almost completed their 17-6 comeback against UCLA, so they can find a way to do the same against Nebraska if needed. The Huskers' defense also needs to be cautious with Oregon's rushing game. Though the Ducks don't strike primarily on the ground, Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison combined for 216 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 54 carries over the last two games, averaging four yards per carry. Though UCLA did suffocate Oregon's run at times, Nebraska could let a play slip by if it's not careful. Oregon's defense also needs to be cautious, seeing how its last two games panned out. The Ducks held USC to 27 points, but Jayden Maiava still threw for 326 yards and two touchdowns on just 23 completions. Oregon also surrendered 205 passing yards on just 13 completions to UCLA, despite holding it to 17 points. Nebraska could do some damage on the run, however. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker tallied 109 rushing yards earlier this season against the Ducks. Anthony Colandrea could do the same and help the Huskers score. Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee all could have moments as well after UCLA's Wayne Knight found some holes in Oregon's defensive line. Knight finished with 103 yards on 22 carries. But this game is also make-or-break for Oregon's postseason hopes, especially with Ohio State and even Northwestern coming up. The Ducks also have a talented roster and, despite their issues, can deliver major blows to opponents when momentum is on their side. Nebraska's issues on the line, in the secondary and even a bit on special teams don't help either. All of this, plus the after-dark setting, provides just enough to tip the scales in the Ducks' favor. Unless Nebraska can truly come out and play like a team that can earn a top-25 spot, this matchup will likely be another so-close-but-so-far loss.
